statement: For 2D rectangular knapsack with bins 900-2000 and 8-12 item types, a maximal-rectangles greedy packer with 6 deterministic orderings (density, value, area, max-dim, total-value, perimeter) x 3 placement methods (BSSF, BAF, BL) plus randomized density-weighted ordering search within 0.75s achieves ~95% of the fractional upper bound.
regime: Bin sizes 900-2000, 8-12 item types, limits up to 2000, 1s time limit
mechanism: MaxRects maintains free rectangle set and greedily places items using best-fit heuristics. Type-level iteration (not per-copy expansion) keeps complexity manageable. Multiple orderings and randomized noise in density-based ordering explore diverse packings.
applicability_bounds: Applies to axis-aligned 2D bin packing with modest type counts (<15) and high per-type limits. May not scale to thousands of distinct types.

statement: Type-level greedy iteration (place all copies of one type before moving to the next) is critical for performance when per-type limits are large (up to 2000). Expanding all copies into a flat candidate list causes TLE.
mechanism: Flat expansion creates O(limit * M) candidates (~24000), causing quadratic free-rect scanning. Type-level iteration processes each type's copies sequentially, exiting early when no fit is found.
applicability_bounds: Relevant when limits are large relative to bin capacity. With small limits this distinction is irrelevant.
